narrative:
Based on the assessment, there is a 42% chance you will fail your final year. Because this exceeds the 10% threshold used to identify students who may need additional support, you are required to enroll in remedial courses. While 42% is not a certainty, it represents a meaningful risk that warrants action.

Three factors most strongly shaped this prediction. The most influential factor actually worked in your favor: you have no history of past class failures, which is a positive signal and pushed the prediction toward passing. This is encouraging and shows you have not struggled with coursework in the same way before.

However, two other factors pushed the prediction in the opposite direction, toward failing. The more significant of these is your weekly study time, which you reported as less than 2 hours. Among students not required to take remedial courses, the vast majority study between 2 and 10 hours per week, with 60% studying 2 to 5 hours alone. Studying so little puts you at a clear disadvantage compared to your peers.

The third factor relates to your father's level of education, which is at primary level. Among students not required to take remedial courses, only about 3% share this background, suggesting that students with less-educated fathers may have access to less academic guidance at home.

The most actionable step you can take right now is to significantly increase your weekly study time. The remedial courses are designed to provide the structured support that can help bridge this gap and improve your chances of passing your final year.
